name: Poster Logo Composer
description: Generates Primary images from a textless TMDb poster with the show/movie logo composited over a blurred (no color tint) fade at the bottom, picking the poster that shows the logo off best. Also saves the logo as the item's Logo image and the best TMDb backdrop as the Backdrop image.
overview: Automatically builds logo-on-poster artwork from TMDb, choosing the textless poster best suited for the logo overlay, and fills in matching Logo/Backdrop images.
changelog:
- Poster scoring now factors in TMDb popularity: added "Poster community rating weight" and "Poster vote count weight" settings (normalized to the same roughly 0-1 scale as flatness/contrast, so they nudge a near-tie rather than dominate). Root cause: the Sherlock poster with a baked-in Kurdish title and "K SERIES" watermark kept winning even after the logo fix and the (opt-in, off-by-default) variance floor, because poster selection never looked at popularity at all — only flatness/contrast/resolution. Checking the actual TMDb candidates confirmed the offending poster was very low resolution and had by far the lowest popularity of the available options, with several other candidates offering equal contrast; a low-resolution upload can score deceptively "flat" simply because downscaling blurred whatever text it had baked in, which flatness alone can't tell apart from a genuinely calm background. Popularity now breaks exactly this kind of tie.
- Fixed the logo counterpart of the previous release's fix ("Monk" kept failing with UnknownImageFormatException even after 1.10.1.0): poster candidates were already tried one-by-one with a fallback to the next if one failed to decode, but logo selection picked exactly one candidate with no fallback at all, so if TMDb's top-ranked logo for an item happened to be undecodable (SVG or otherwise — the URL-extension check alone wasn't catching every case), the whole item failed every run with no way to recover. Logo selection now ranks the full fallback order (same language → language-neutral → English → any-language, each tier internally ranked as before) and tries each one in turn, downloading *and* verifying it actually decodes, falling through to the next candidate on any failure instead of giving up on the first bad one.
- Fixed a crash ("Failed to compose Primary image", UnknownImageFormatException) whenever TMDb served an SVG poster or logo candidate — ImageSharp (used for compositing) has no vector-image decoder and threw on it. SVG candidates are now filtered out before selection/download, at the single point where all TMDb images are gathered, so poster/logo selection never considers one in the first place.
- Added an opt-in safety floor ("Max poster band variance", off by default) for the case where TMDb mistags a poster as textless (`language == null`) when it actually has baked-in text/logos/branding — e.g. a foreign streaming service's own release image with its own title and branding burned in (observed on a Sherlock poster carrying a Kurdish title and a "K SERIES" watermark baked into the image itself). If even the best-scoring textless candidate's bottom-band luminance variance exceeds the configured ceiling, Primary generation is now skipped for that item entirely instead of compositing the logo on top of someone else's branding. Existing flatness-based selection already prefers calmer candidates, but had no hard floor for when nothing better is available.
- Added a last-resort, localized contrast backdrop: even with correct poster selection (1.9.1.0), some titles (e.g. American Sniper) simply have no textless TMDb poster candidate with good natural contrast for the logo, so the best available pick can still read weakly (thin serif strokes blending into a bright sky, etc.). If the poster actually chosen still falls short of a minimum logo/band luminance gap (new "Minimum contrast gap" setting, default 70), a soft, heavily-feathered backdrop is now drawn as a fallback — but scoped tightly to the logo's own footprint (with padding) rather than the whole band, and capped by a new "Max localized backdrop strength" setting. A well-matched pairing (the common case) gets no backdrop at all, and even a poorly-matched one never turns into the old flat, hard-edged rectangle over a solid-color background, since it's small, centered on the logo, and fades out well before the band's edges. Set "Minimum contrast gap" to 0 to disable and rely purely on poster selection.
- Fixed poor logo/background contrast (e.g. a white logo on a light/bright poster, as seen on American Sniper and The Accountant): poster scoring predicted contrast assuming the band would be darkened toward black by up to "Max gradient strength" behind the logo — a leftover assumption from before 1.8.0.0, which removed that darkening/tint entirely (blur-only fade). The prediction never got updated, so a bright poster could still score as "good contrast" for a white logo even though nothing was ever drawn to darken it. Contrast is now scored against the poster's real, unaltered band luminance, matching what actually gets rendered. The now-dead "Max gradient strength" setting has been removed.
- Logo selection no longer picks the highest-resolution candidate outright: within each language tier, candidates at or above a configurable minimum width ("Minimum logo width", default 1000px) now compete on community rating/vote count instead, with resolution only breaking ties; if nothing reaches that width the requirement is dropped (not the item) and the same rating-first pick runs over every candidate. Applies to the language-matched, language-neutral, English and any-language-fallback tiers alike. New "Logo community rating weight" / "Logo vote count weight" settings tune it.
- Removed the black/white color tint entirely, based on real-world examples (a Game of Thrones and a Brooklyn Nine-Nine poster) where it turned into a visibly odd-colored, flat rectangle over solid-color/textureless poster backgrounds (bright yellow, near-black) — there was no texture for the tint to blend into, so even a "needs-based", small amount of it stood out badly. Also fixed a sign error in the (now removed) direction logic while investigating. The fade is now blur-only, with no added color; logo/background contrast is handled entirely by poster selection (Contrast weight).
- Fixed a remaining hard edge in the fade: the blur itself was applied to a hard-edged rectangle, causing a visible sharp-to-blurry seam at the band's top edge independent of the darkening/lightening fade. The blur now cross-fades in smoothly from the untouched poster above it, verified against a synthetic high-frequency test image and real posters.
- Shrunk the default fade band from 35% to 22% of the poster's height, and decoupled the logo's max size from the band height (now a fraction of the poster's height instead), so the fade covers noticeably less of the poster while the logo stays the same size — the logo may now extend above the fade band itself; only the part overlapping the band gets blurred/faded.
- Fixed a visible hard-edged "bar" appearing behind some logos (e.g. Assassin's Creed's dark logo on its near-white poster): the fade was always applied at a fixed strength even when the poster/logo pairing already had excellent natural contrast, darkening an already-perfect area into a visible rectangle — and unconditionally darkening actively hurt contrast for dark-colored logos rather than helping. The fade now only kicks in when needed: it compares the logo's brightness against the poster band's brightness and only fades (toward whichever of black/white increases the gap) by just enough to reach a configurable target contrast (new "Target contrast gap" setting) capped by the existing max-strength setting — a well-matched poster/logo pairing now gets little or no fade at all. Verified against real TMDb assets (Assassin's Creed, 6 different logos).
- Reworked contrast handling based on feedback that the adaptive (sometimes white) fade from 1.5.0.0 looked inconsistent — a plain white block behind some logos. The fade is now always the same black darkening everywhere in the library (kept fairly subtle/transparent by default), and instead the poster *selection* itself is now contrast-aware: each candidate poster is scored on how much contrast this specific logo is predicted to have against its bottom band once the fade is applied, alongside the existing flatness/resolution scoring (new "Contrast weight" setting). A white logo will now be matched with a poster whose band stays dark enough, rather than the fade trying to compensate after the fact.
- Fixed logo language fallback picking an unrelated language (e.g. a Chinese logo in a German library) whenever no logo matched the library's language or a language-neutral one: the last resort was "any logo, highest resolution wins" regardless of language. It now tries English as an additional, more sensible fallback, and by default skips the item entirely rather than using an unrelated-language logo. The old behavior (always use *some* logo) is available again via the new "Allow any-language logo as a last resort" setting.
- Fixed poor contrast between the logo and its backdrop (e.g. a white logo on a white/light poster): the fade gradient is now adaptive — it darkens (black) behind a bright/light-colored logo or lightens (white) behind a dark-colored logo, whichever gives better contrast, and it now reaches full configured strength right at the logo's own position (with a smooth feather above it) instead of a flat top-to-bottom ease that often left the logo itself barely treated. New "Gradient feather" setting controls the transition width.
- Fixed the root cause found via the 1.4.1.0 diagnostics: this TMDb provider marks "no language" images with an empty string ("") rather than an actual null value, so the textless-poster filter (and the language-neutral logo fallback) never matched anything and Primary images silently stopped being generated, even though Logo and Backdrop kept working. Both filters now treat null and empty string as "no language" alike.
- Diagnostic release: Primary/poster images silently stop being generated for some setups while Logo and Backdrop keep working (no error, just no "Generating composed Primary image" log line). Added Information-level logging that reports, per item, how many Primary candidates TMDb actually returned and what languages they carry, plus whether the TMDb provider even lists Primary among its supported image types for that item — this will pinpoint the cause on the next run.
- Added "Automatically use each library's preferred metadata language for the logo" (on by default): the logo language is now taken from each item's library settings (falling back to the server default language), instead of always using a single fixed language. The manually configured language is still used as a fallback and can be selected exclusively by turning auto-detection off.
- Fixed: Backdrop images no longer accumulate on every task run (a null image index appended a new Backdrop instead of replacing one) — the number of Backdrops is now capped by the new "Max backdrops to keep" setting, and existing Backdrops beyond that count are cleared out each run.
- Fixed: TMDb image URLs are now rewritten to request the original (full) resolution before downloading, since some TMDb provider setups returned a downscaled preview (e.g. 500x750) even when the source poster was much larger (e.g. 1500x3000). Toggle via the new "Always download TMDb images at original resolution" setting.
- Fetches images directly from the TMDb image provider instead of going through the library's enabled/disabled "image fetcher" list, so this works even if TMDb image fetching is turned off for Primary/Logo/Backdrop in a library's settings (recommended, to stop regular scans from overwriting the generated images) — and no longer triggers other, unrelated providers (e.g. a broken TheTVDB call) in the process.
- Also saves the logo used for the Primary composite as the item's own Logo image.
- Also selects and saves the highest resolution, best rated TMDb backdrop as the Backdrop image.
- Initial release: scheduled task that composes a Primary image per movie/series from the best-fitting textless TMDb poster and the item's logo, blurred and faded in at the bottom.
